related_questions.question: What do US citizens need to travel to the UK?

text_blocks.snippet: U.S. citizens traveling to the UK need an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) or a visa, depending on the purpose and length of their stay. For short visits, tourism, or business, an ETA is generally required starting January 8, 2025. If the visit is longer than six months or for other purposes like work or study, a visa may be necessary.
snippet_highlighted_words: an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) or a visa

list.title: Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA):
list.snippet: U.S. citizens will need an ETA for travel to or through the UK, including Northern Ireland, for short visits (tourism, business, family visits, or transit). This requirement is similar to the US ESTA and applies from January 8, 2025.

list.title: Visas:
list.snippet: Visas are required for longer stays (more than six months), work, study, or other specific purposes that are not covered by the ETA.

list.title: Passport:
list.snippet: A valid passport is required for all travelers, and it should be valid for the duration of the visit, according to the UK government.

list.title: Applying for an ETA:
list.snippet: You can apply for an ETA online through the UK government website.

list.title: Applying for a Visa:
list.snippet: If a visa is needed, it must be applied for online before travel and may involve an interview at a visa application center, according to the UK government.

list.title: Transiting through the UK:
list.snippet: Even if you are just changing flights at a UK airport, you may need an ETA or visa, depending on your nationality and circumstances.

list.title: Children:
list.snippet: Children and young people (under 18) may need a valid visa or ETA, and may also need additional documentation like a letter of consent from their parents, says GOV.UK.
